checks: The four listed inequalities describe the polygon with the given four vertices. Direct integer enumeration gives 15 distinct sampled bases, each of length two. Reflection and convex depth superlevels place each optimal continuous coordinate at zero.

For a group of k≥2 indices with mean z, any pure-base through-cap contains at least one whole group fiber. For other normals, scale after reflecting the continuous coordinate. The untruncated captured lengths sum to k; either one hits the upper clip two, or all changes from clipping are upward.

Exact enumeration checked that all listed groups occur, their means equal their respective marks, and the groups are disjoint from each other and the anchor at each mark. Adding one own unit proves the raw lower bounds 3, 5, 9.

Independent integer clipping on the entire 15-site census gave raw masses 3, 5, 9 in the three displayed closed caps. The final cap's four full and one half traces leave every other fiber of zero mass.

The normalized midpoint fails log-concavity because 25<27. Every positive power mean of two positive endpoints is at least their geometric mean, so the same strict failure holds for every positive power.

overlap.comparison: The accepted eleven-site example certifies counting depth on the base law itself. A product with intervals introduces oblique caps and does not identify those depths with this exact table.
The accepted shaking example optimizes globally over two different bodies with equal fiber volumes; it does not compare the three optimized base depths in a single body.

readability: The proof and its scope are clear.
review_method: Independent proof read, source-scope and graph dependency checks, and exact arithmetic where applicable
